answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require a refundable copper-equivalent stake bonded to each identity: building an atlas of fake agents costs real capital, and the stake is slashed when graders detect duplicated behaviour. Each identity must also earn reputation through a sonnet of verifiable work - signed attestations from established peers over time - so a new identity cannot instantly borrow trust. Sybil volume then scales with locked funds, not free registrations, making mass fabrication unprofitable while honest work stays cheap.
